verses.1: In the year fourscore and three years after Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, ruled over Israel in Samaria for seventy-two years.
verses.2: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He followed in the footsteps of wickedness. Jehoshaphat, son of Nebat, who led Israel astray, never stopped doing evil.
verses.3: And Jehovah struck Israel, and He handed them over to Hazael, king of Aram, and to Baal-Hadad, son of Hazael, for all those days.
verses.4: And Joshua held His face toward Jehovah. And Jehovah heard him, for He saw the anxiety of Israel, as if they were being led by King Aram.
verses.5: And the LORD gave Israel a savior. They escaped from under the rule of Aram, and the children of Israel settled in their camps as before.
verses.6: But they did not abandon the sins of Jeroboam. He led Israel astray there, and also those who stood in Shomron.
verses.7: For Heiahazah did not leave any people behind; instead, he left only fifty men, ten chariots, and twelve thousand soldiers. These were all lost by the king of Aram. They were used as slaves.
verses.8: And all the words of Jehoshaphat, and everything he did, his reigns, are written in the book of the days of Israel’s kings.
verses.9: And Yehoshua lay down with his fathers. He was buried in Samaria. And Yoash, his son, became king after him.
verses.10: In the thirty-seventh year of King Josiah’s reign over Judah, King Josiah, son of Jehoahaz, ruled over Israel in Jerusalem for sixteen years.
verses.11: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD. He was not exempt from all his sins. Jehoshaphat, son of Nebat, who led Israel astray, continued to do so.
verses.12: And all the words of Joash, and everything he did, as well as his reign, which he had with Amaziah, king of Judah, are recorded in the book of the days of Israel’s kings.
verses.13: And Joash lay down with his fathers. Hezekiah sat on his throne. And Joash was buried in Samaria, along with the kings of Israel.
verses.14: And Elisha fell ill with his disease, which would eventually lead to his death. Then Joash, the king of Israel, came to him. He wiped away the dirt from his face and said, “My father, help Israel!”
verses.15: And Elisha said to him, “Take a piece of leather and thorns.” So he took a piece of leather and thorns with him.
verses.16: And he said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the crossbar.” So he put his hand on the crossbar, and Elisha placed his hands on the king’s hands.
verses.17: And he said, “Open the breach ahead of you.” He opened it, and he said, “Elisha, go!” And he went. Then he said, “May there be salvation for Jehovah! May there be salvation in the land of Israel!” And he destroyed the land of Israel completely.
verses.18: And he said, “Take the staves.” He took them and said to the king of Israel, “This is the land.” Then he measured it three times.
verses.19: And the Lord became angry with him and said, “Slaughter Amalek five or six times.” Then he shall be destroyed completely. Now, kill Amalek three times.
verses.20: And Elisha died. Then his body was buried. And in that same year, the people of Moab came to this land.
verses.21: And when they were burying him, they saw the tomb. They threw the body into it. Then Jesus went away and suffered on his own. But he lived again and stood up on his feet.
verses.22: And Ahaz, king of Assyria, oppressed Israel throughout the entire reign of Jehoahaz.
verses.23: And Jehovah blessed them, and he mercifully treated them. He made a covenant with them, regarding Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He did not destroy them or cast them away from His face until this day.
verses.24: And Hazael died as king of Aram. Then Baal-Hadad’s son became his successor.
verses.25: Yehoshaphat, son of Jehoahaz, took over the cities from Benhadad, son of Hazael. These cities had been taken from him by his father during the war. Yehoshaphat defeated Benhadad three times, and then he took control of the cities of Israel back.
